newsitem.title: CHINA: Daimler-Benz silent on reported China delay.
newsitem.headline: Daimler-Benz silent on reported China delay.

text.p: Officials of German industrial group Daimler-Benz AG declined to comment on Tuesday on a report of delays to a a proposed $1.0 billion joint venture with two Chinese automobile firms.
"We are still working very hard on this project," an official of the Daimler Benz office in Beijing said by telephone.

An official reached at Nanfang Automotive Corp, one of the Chinese firms involved in the project, also declined to comment on the report by the Hong Kong South China Morning Post newspaper, saying the project was still in the planning stages.
"This project is just being planned, sometimes plans are late, sometimes early. You can't say this has been delayed," the official said.

The South China Morning Post said on Tuesday disputes between Nanfang Automotive Corp, a subsidiary of Guangdong Sanxing Enterprise (Group) Co Ltd, and the Hainan Automotive Factory had delayed the $1.0 billion venture.

"The Chinese partners in the venture have been locked in a prolonged wrangle over financing, the right to assemble certain parts, and the medium and long-term development plans," the Post said, quoting unidentified sources.
The newspaper said the project was still waiting for approval from China's State Planning Commission and would almost certainly be delayed beyond the scheduled 1998 start-up date.

Mercedes Benz, the vehicle production unit of Daimler Benz, last year beat off several international rivals to sign a feasibility study agreement with China to set up two plants in the southern provinces of Hainan and Guangdong.
Under preliminary agreements, Mercedes would hold a 45 percent stake in the project, which is to produce 60,000 luxury vans and 100,000 diesel engines a year.
